report:
Reviewed the complete canonical_boundary claim, three ordinary implementation associations, four ordinary tests and one TODO test. Requirements: canonicalize goal and environment together; preserve rigid/flexible inputs, relative universes, substitutions, residuals and goal-specific outputs without capture or lost sharing; apply knowledge transactionally; import normalization output before relating it to caller expectation. Captured inference design and linked architectural-foundations rationale for output-producing solver operations.

canonical.rs uses one Canonicalizer for assumptions followed by SolverGoal. It maps free rigid identities and egraph-root flexible variables through shared maps, carries kind/role/domain/universe metadata, subtracts a common universe base, and keeps the inverse caller mapping outside the query data. Nested existential binders receive distinct alpha identities with saved/restored lexical mappings. Shared traversal of types, aliases, predicates and assumptions retains repeated input identities. The canonical goal stores Normalize(alias), not an expected output type. infer_ctx canonicalize_obligation_goal likewise omits expected from the solver goal.

boundary.rs instantiate_query creates an isolated proof stash/egraph, recreates rigid placeholders and flexible inputs with their canonical universes/domains, and copies environment and goal through one mapping. ResponseExtractor traverses substitutions, output and residuals using shared response-variable maps. It reuses an input class only when the resolved root still has the original domain and universe; critically this compares the root variable's current universe, not an obsolete unified input index. Changed ceilings/domains therefore become response-bound variables and substitutions. Response-local variables carry relative universe/domain metadata. Extraction checks operation/output compatibility for successful results and asserts no proof-local inference variable escapes. IrCopier copies output/substitutions/residuals through the same map and freshens residual binders with lexical save/restore.

apply_query_response validates mapping arity, substitution keys and response binder identities, allocates imports in a child egraph version, applies substitutions there, and collapses only after all unifications succeed; errors discard the branch. Captured egraph branch/collapse/discard and unifier excerpts confirm universe ceilings and class changes are child state and are merged only on success. apply_normalization_relation creates an outer transaction, imports the solver response first, then unifies the returned Type with expected. Maybe/No/import failure/relation failure discard that outer transaction; successful relation publishes commit effects. This ordering prevents expected from selecting the normalized candidate. Captured goal/result definitions make the distinct output and residual fields explicit.

Supported-input limitation investigated: canonicalization has Const::Param handling, but IrCopier's const mapping is narrower. This is not claimed supported const round-trip behavior: captured goal.rs validation rejects const-parameter arrays, rejects non-type existential inputs/binders, and captured prove.rs solve_query validates before instantiation/execution. Captured trait_env.rs explicitly marks const-generic declarations Unsupported. Thus the suspected free-const remapping path is outside admitted solver inputs; no supported-input behavioral failure was identified. Root agreed with this restriction-based assessment. Enabling those inputs later requires completing remapping and its tests; this report does not broaden current support.

All ordinary tests read in full: canonical_equality_round_trips_transactionally constructs a boundary equality, instantiates/unifies/extracts/applies it and asserts Yes plus the caller variable resolving to i32. It establishes successful substitution application, not rollback on failure. canonical_response_preserves_lowered_input_universe lowers a proof input's universe and asserts the caller ceiling becomes Universe(1). canonical_response_preserves_lowered_unified_input_universe first unifies two proof inputs, lowers the representative, then asserts both caller inputs share a root and that root has the lowered ceiling. These directly cover the original-input and aliased-input metadata paths. response_local_type_output_round_trips_with_sharing obtains a normalization result with one response-bound variable, imports a tuple output, checks trivial residual, equal inference IDs in both tuple elements, and root universe. Its deliberately unconstrained generic impl fixture and manually constructed query exercise boundary mechanics; they are not evidence of acceptance of that program by rustc or a full body-level normalization scenario. Captured source fixture and trait/associated-item lookup helpers show production source parsing and symbol discovery; the low-level manually constructed egraph portions are treated as focused boundary tests.

The TODO inference_canonical_boundary explicitly retains the larger matrix: rigid/flexible inputs, nested binders, universes, shared response locals, residual obligations, type outputs, and incompatible expected type not choosing among ambiguous normalization candidates. It has no assertions. Completing it requires admitted-input source-backed scenarios and targeted transactional failure/ambiguity cases, plus binder/residual sharing and capture assertions; unsupported const kinds additionally require implementation support first. The four tests are useful partial evidence and do not close that TODO. No N/A evidence applies.

Executed fresh review start with coordinator instructions, source inspection, and review read captures of design/RFD, query/result types, fixture helpers, transaction/unifier helpers and supported-input restrictions. No test commands or build executed by this reviewer; central suite results are separate. No source edits. No requested edits; explicitly retained verification and input-support limits remain visible.
